timeline_events.summary: Mahmoud Ahmadinejad took office as President of Iran, after which his government imposed crackdowns that plunged publishing into crisis.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad won Iran's presidential election.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, as Tehran mayor since 2003, ran for president with an ascetic, man-of-the-people campaign appealing to religious hardliners and working-class conservatives.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad is elected president of Iran.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, the ultra-conservative mayor of Tehran, was accused of ballot-rigging after unexpectedly winning his way into a run-off vote in Iran's presidential election.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, the ultra-hardline mayor of Tehran, advances to a second-round runoff in Iran's presidential election amid allegations of electoral malpractice, which he denies.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad wins Iran's presidential runoff election, defeating Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani.

Mahmoud Ahmadinejad was newly elected as Iran's hardline president, with his inauguration expected the following month, amid speculation that top nuclear negotiator Hassan Rowhani would resign before it.
Iranian president-elect Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's aides dismiss allegations that he was involved in the 1989 assassination of exiled Kurdish politician Abdul Rahman Ghassemlou in Vienna.

Iran's president-elect Mahmoud Ahmadinejad received religious approval from Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, taking his first step toward assuming office ahead of his formal inauguration on Saturday.
Iran's new president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad announced the make-up of his cabinet, naming a team of religious conservatives to key ministries.
Iran's conservative-dominated parliament rejected four of President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's proposed cabinet ministers, including his nominee for oil minister, Ali Saeedlou.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, in a meeting with the British, French, and German foreign ministers, rejected threats of sanctions and asserted Iran would press ahead with its nuclear program.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad meets the leaders of Britain, France and Germany in New York to discuss Iran's nuclear activities and avoid possible UN Security Council referral.

Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad stated at a summit in New York that Iran would not give up its entitlement to enrich uranium, though he offered to open enrichment operations to foreign companies and countries.
Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad reiterated his prediction of Israel's demise at a Jerusalem Day rally, remarks that drew widespread condemnation.
Iran proposes reopening nuclear talks with EU countries, a move seen as an effort to ease diplomatic pressure following President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's call to "wipe Israel off the map."

An informed Iranian source says President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad has divided the clerical establishment and alienated moderates, with his comment that Israel should be "wiped off the map" and his purges of senior officials drawing rebukes at home.
Iran's parliament rejected President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's third nominee for oil minister, Mohsen Tasalloti, deepening a crisis over control of the strategically sensitive post.
Iran's parliament approved Kazem Vaziri-Hamaneh as oil minister, a compromise after MPs rejected two of President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's previous choices and a third withdrew.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad became the first senior Iranian official to openly deny the Holocaust, describing it as a "myth" in a speech in Zahedan.

Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad defiantly stated that Iran would press ahead with its nuclear programme despite international threats and outcry over its decision to break UN seals at the Natanz enrichment facility.
President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad is cracking down on Iran's universities to crush a student pro-democracy movement and strengthen hardliners' grip on power.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad made a triumphal announcement regarding Iran's nuclear program, accompanied by chants of "Death to America" and "Death to Israel."
The Simon Wiesenthal Centre calls on Germany to ban Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad from attending the World Cup, urging Fifa to bar him from the tournament.
Iran announces it has successfully enriched uranium to a new level of 4.8%, a month after President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad revealed enrichment to 3.6%.

Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad said he was ready to discuss "mutual concerns" over Tehran's nuclear programme but warned his country would not respond to threats, without saying whether he would accept a Western package of incentives.

Iranian officials and Western diplomats say Mahmoud Ahmadinejad’s popularity is surging almost a year after his presidential election win, with support attributed to his populist style and stance on the nuclear issue.
Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad launched a blog aimed at an international audience, with his first post asking readers whether the US and Israel intended to start a new world war.
Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad launches his personal blog, with his first posting describing his early life.
Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad started his own blog this week and launched an online vote asking whether US and Israeli actions against Lebanon are pulling the trigger for another world war.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad launched a blog attached to his presidential website.

UN Secretary General Kofi Annan said that Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad reaffirmed Iran's preparedness and determination to negotiate a solution to the nuclear crisis, while stating Iran does not accept suspension of uranium enrichment before negotiations.
Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad called for a purge of "liberal and secular" academics in universities.
A censorship crackdown instigated by President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad led to the banning of dozens of literary masterpieces and international bestsellers in Iran.

Iranian students protested against President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad at Tehran's Amir Kabir university, burning his picture and chanting "Death to the dictator," in the first sign of open dissent since he took office.
Iranian voters went to the polls to elect local councils and the Assembly of Experts in the first test of President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's popularity since he took office.

Ahmadinejad's supporters apparently failed to win control of key councils in elections, with his Sweet Scent of Service coalition winning only three of 15 Tehran city council seats, while critic Hashemi Rafsanjani received the most votes in elections to the experts' assembly.
150 Iranian parliamentarians signed a letter blaming President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad for raging inflation and high unemployment and criticizing his government's failure to deliver the budget on time.
A majority of Iran's MPs sign an open letter to President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad criticizing his economic policies.

Hashemi Rafsanjani, Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's political rival, met Britain's ambassador to Tehran and indicated Iran was willing to submit to verification measures regarding its nuclear programme, challenging Ahmadinejad's defiant stance.
An Iranian website critical of President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad is shut down in an apparent crackdown on anti-government dissent online.
An Iranian website critical of President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad is shut down in an apparent crackdown on anti-government dissent on the internet.

Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad delivered a defiant speech defending Iran's nuclear projects and said Iran would resist "all bullies" and continue its nuclear program, amid rising tensions with the West over new UN sanctions.

Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad came under domestic criticism from political commentators, reformists, and even a usually supportive fundamentalist newspaper for his uncompromising rhetoric on the nuclear issue, with critics saying his remarks made it harder for Iran's top nuclear negotiator to reach a compromise with European diplomats.

Students who protested against Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad at Tehran's Amir Kabir University in December were expelled and earmarked for compulsory military service in an apparent act of official retribution.

Iranian students who protested against President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad in December have been expelled from Tehran's Amir Kabir University and earmarked for compulsory military service in an apparent act of official retribution.
Thousands of teachers protested against President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's economic policies outside Iran's parliament, despite police arresting six trade union leaders the previous day.
Tehran Mayor Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf is re-elected in a vote seen as a sign of waning support for hardline President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad.

Mahmoud Ahmadinejad appoints a 15-member advisory council to compile his "works and opinions" for commercial publication, though two selected advisers declined to participate because they had not been consulted in advance.
Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad turned down a request by American film director Oliver Stone to make a documentary about him, dismissing Stone as "part of the Great Satan."

Allies of Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad accuse the media of attempting a "creeping coup" to depose him, amid reports he authorized a special team to counter "black propaganda against the government."

Iran's fundamentalist-dominated parliament passes a law severely restricting political advertising for the March 2008 parliamentary elections, which are expected to test Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's popularity.
Iranian authorities closed down the reformist newspaper Shargh, which had been critical of President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, in the latest stage of an offensive against his opponents in the media.
Iranian authorities shut down the leading reformist newspaper Shargh, which had been critical of President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, in the latest stage of an offensive against his opponents in the media.

International day of action protests take place in more than 30 countries in solidarity with Iran's trade union movement, highlighting the jailing of union leader Mansour Osanloo under the government of President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad.
Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad is establishing a hotline for ordinary citizens to voice problems, complaints, and proposals, to be launched next February during the Fajr festival.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad denied the existence of homosexuals in Iran at Columbia University, prompting journalist Siamak Ghaderi to conduct interviews with Iranian homosexuals.

Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad is poised to deliver a defiant address to the UN General Assembly amid protests over his visit to New York, and Iran's military unveiled a new long-range ballistic missile called the Ghadr.
Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad dismissed talk of a US or Israeli air strike on Iran as a propaganda tool during a visit to New York for a UN General Assembly meeting.

Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, Iran's president, spoke at Columbia University, denying Iran has a nuclear weapons program and claiming Iran has no homosexuals, after being denounced by the university president as a "petty and cruel dictator."
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad claims at a New York event that there are no homosexuals in Iran, drawing criticism from human rights lawyers and international gay rights activists.
Following Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's visit to Columbia University in the US, an Iranian university invites George Bush to answer questions from its students and teachers.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad is losing political strength inside Iran as rivals gain power and economic conditions decline, though he retains influence over the economy.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad labeled his domestic opponents "traitors" working for the West and threatened to expose them, escalating tensions over Iran's nuclear policy.

Reformist newspaper Etemad reports that Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's blog has attracted scathing criticism from respondents, including sarcastic messages about petrol rationing, high unemployment, and high inflation.
Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad offers himself as an observer for the 2008 US presidential election, claiming Americans would vote against the current administration in a truly free poll.

An Iranian court acquits former nuclear negotiator Hossein Mousavian of spying for the British government but convicts him of acting against the Islamic authorities, after President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad had called him a "spy" and "traitor."
Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei overruled President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad by ordering him to supply cheap gas to villages amid power cuts during an unusually harsh winter.
Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad arrived in Baghdad on the first state visit of its kind since the 1979 Islamic revolution, pledging a new chapter in relations with Iraq.

In Iran's parliamentary elections, hardline conservatives—including critics of President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad—appeared to have secured up to 70% of seats, with pro-Ahmadinejad hard-liners winning 42 of the 115 seats decided so far.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad described Saturday's international talks on Iran's nuclear programme as a "step forward," although Western officials said the negotiations ended in deadlock.
Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei told a cabinet meeting that President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad should prepare for a second term in office ahead of June's presidential election.
An ally of Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad says he has fallen ill due to exhaustion from his heavy workload, amid doubts over whether he will seek re-election in 2009.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad delivered Channel 4's alternative Christmas Day broadcast, in which he said Jesus Christ will return together with one of the children of the Messenger of Islam.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad was re-elected president of Iran after a disputed vote.
Swiss ambassador Livia Leu Agosti is expected to present her diplomatic credentials to President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad in the coming weeks.

Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad responded acerbically to Barack Obama's overture to Iran, saying only "fundamental" change from Washington—including a complete withdrawal of US troops worldwide and apologies for past "crimes" against Iran—would be enough to reboot bilateral relations after a 30-year freeze.
Reformist former Iranian president Mohammed Khatami is close to declaring his candidacy for June's presidential election against incumbent Mahmoud Ahmadinejad.
Iran's president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad is expected to claim major progress in the country's nuclear programme on Iran's nuclear technology day, at a critical moment in US-Iranian relations.
Iran celebrates National Nuclear Technology Day, with President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad expected to give a yearly speech about Iran's nuclear accomplishments ahead of the June 12 presidential elections.
Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad returned home to an officially described warm welcome after his speech at a UN anti-racism conference in Geneva, where he described Israel as a racist state.
Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad replicated Barack Obama's "Yes We Can" campaign slogan in a promotional video for Iran's presidential election.
Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad officially declared that he would run for a second term in the upcoming election.
Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad declared during a visit to the US that "in Iran there are no homosexuals like in America," sparking a media frenzy, and he later clarified his words.

Iran's culture ministry closes the reformist newspaper Yas-e-No, affiliated with Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's rival Mir-Hossein Moussavi, amid a censorship drive by Ahmadinejad's government ahead of the June 12 presidential election.
Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad said he would rebut increasingly strident criticisms from reformist candidates opposing him in the country's presidential elections.
Iran intensified internet censorship following protests over the presidential election results attributed to Mahmoud Ahmadinejad.

Mojtaba Khamenei, an ally of Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, is reported to have been a driving force behind the government crackdown and was credited with securing his father's endorsement for Ahmadinejad in the 2005 elections.

Mahmoud Ahmadinejad participated in an unprecedented live televised debate with rival Mir Hussein Mousavi ahead of Iran's June 12 presidential election, during which Mousavi criticized Ahmadinejad's foreign policy, press clampdowns, and personal attacks.
Zahra Rahnavard, wife of opposition candidate Mir Hossein Mousavi, threatens to sue Mahmoud Ahmadinejad for lying about her educational qualifications ahead of Iran's presidential election.

Mahmoud Ahmadinejad held a large rally in Tehran, but his bodyguards prevented him from speaking due to chaotic security arrangements, as rival Mir Hossein Mousavi mounted a massive show of strength ahead of Friday's presidential poll.

Former president Ali Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani publicly accused President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad of lying during a televised election debate and urged Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei to rein him in ahead of Friday's poll.
On the eve of Iran's presidential election, Mahmoud Ahmadinejad uses his final campaign rally to attack Zionism and imperialism and accuse his rivals of using "Hitler's methods."

Iranians vote in a presidential election in which incumbent Mahmoud Ahmadinejad faces a strong challenge from moderate candidate Mir Hossein Mousavi, with experts predicting Mousavi would likely win if the result is not rigged.

Official results declare Mahmoud Ahmadinejad the winner of Iran's presidential election with 63% of the vote, a result disputed by opposition candidate Mirhossein Mousavi who alleges the true result was leaked showing he won over 60%.

Iran's electoral commission said Mahmoud Ahmadinejad had taken 69% of the vote after 5 million were counted, while challenger Mir-Hossein Mousavi claimed he had won and complained of widespread irregularities.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad was confirmed as the winner of Iran's presidential election, sparking violent clashes in Tehran.
Defeated Iranian presidential candidate Mir Hossein Mousavi lodges a formal appeal against the election result that returned Mahmoud Ahmadinejad to power, as protests continue in Tehran.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's re-election as Iranian President is disputed, with accusations of vote rigging.

Mahmoud Ahmadinejad traveled to Yekaterinburg, Russia for a Shanghai Co-operation Organisation summit amid anti-government protests over Iran's disputed presidential election, where the SCO formally congratulated him on his landslide win.
At least 500 activists, opposition figures, journalists, and students have been arrested in Iran in a growing crackdown aimed at "decapitating" the movement against Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's re-election.

Iranian security forces threatened a "decisive and revolutionary confrontation" with opposition demonstrators continuing protests against Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's claimed victory in the presidential elections.
Iran imposes life bans on four footballers who wore green wristbands in a World Cup match in protest against Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's disputed re-election.

Iranian media report that Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, winner of the disputed presidential election, is to be sworn in before parliament between 26 July and 19 August, after Iran's top electoral authority rules out annulling the result.
Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad orders an investigation into the killing of Neda Agha Soltan, calling her death a "suspicious" and "heartfelt event."

Mahmoud Ahmadinejad hails his contested re-election as a victory for the Iranian people and a defeat for the enemies of the Islamic Republic, after the Guardian Council confirmed his defeat of challenger Mir Hossein Mousavi.
Hassan Khomeini, grandson of Ayatollah Khomeini, reportedly left Iran to avoid attending Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's presidential inauguration.
Mir Hossein Mousavi declared the new government of Mahmoud Ahmadinejad "illegitimate" following the disputed presidential election.
The Assembly of Scholars and Researchers at Qom seminary rejects Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's re-election as "illegitimate" and calls for the release of political prisoners.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad delivers a live state television address defending his re-election as a democratic triumph and mocking opponents for failing to provide evidence of vote fraud.
Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei reportedly orders President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad to sack his newly appointed first vice-president, Esfandiar Rahim-Mashai.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad announced his intention to appoint three women cabinet members, including Fatemeh Ajorlou as social welfare minister and Marzieh Vahid Dastjerdi as health minister.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's endorsement ceremony for a second term was boycotted by senior clerics, political luminaries, and opposition figures, with celebrities invited to fill the empty seats.
Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei formally endorsed Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's second term as president, seven weeks after disputed elections prompted mass protests.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad formally began his second term as Iran's president, pledging to serve his people and resist foreign powers questioning the validity of his election.

Iranian president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad nominated three women to his cabinet, including Fatemeh Ajorlou as social welfare minister and Marzieh Vahid Dastjerdi as health minister, and said Heydar Moslehi would be nominated as intelligence minister.

Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad proposes three women for his new cabinet, including Fatemeh Ajorlou for the welfare and social security ministry and Marzieh Vahid Dastjerdi for the health ministry.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad nominates Ahmad Vahidi, a former Revolutionary Guards commander wanted by Interpol for the 1994 Buenos Aires Jewish centre bombing, to head Iran's defence ministry.
President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's cabinet nominees are reported to be dominated by loyalists linked to the Revolutionary Guards, including three women, with many strongly tied to the IRGC.
Iranian authorities launched a purge against student activists to prevent protests against President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's re-election, jailing some students and suspending others.

Mahmoud Ahmadinejad won parliamentary approval for 18 of his cabinet nominees, including a defence minister wanted in Argentina over a 1994 terrorist attack and Iran's first female minister since the Islamic revolution.

Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad repeated his claim that the Nazi Holocaust was a "lie" during a Tehran University speech, as opposition protesters gathered in central Tehran chanting "death to the dictator."
Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad faced walkouts at the UN General Assembly after accusing Israel of genocide, barbarism, and racism in a speech.

Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad faces ongoing domestic political tensions and uncertainty following the disputed June presidential election, as internal debates over electoral reform continue and opposition protests persist despite a crackdown.

An article disputes claims that Mahmoud Ahmadinejad has Jewish roots, arguing his family were religious Shia Muslims and that his previous surname Sabourjian derived from carpet-thread painting, not a Jewish prayer shawl.

Prominent reformists remain in detention after Iran's post-election turmoil, with some having made televised confessions that claims of electoral fraud against President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad were unfounded.
A revolutionary court in Tehran sentenced Mohammad Reza Ali-Zamani to death for involvement in mass protests against President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's disputed re-election.
Students across Iran are planning to lead a huge day of protest against President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's regime, commemorating the 30th anniversary of the US embassy takeover.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad begins a South American tour in Brazil, where he is greeted by protests and is expected to hold talks with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad won a second term in office, after which protests occurred and a protester was shot dead in December 2009.

The funeral of reformist cleric Grand Ayatollah Hossein Ali Montazeri in Qom became a rallying point for protests against the disputed re-election of Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, with hundreds of thousands of mourners chanting anti-government slogans.
Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad blamed America and Israel for widespread anti-government protests around the holy mourning day of Ashura.

Mahmoud Ahmadinejad offered to relaunch negotiations over Iran's uranium stockpile, saying Iran had no problem sending enriched uranium abroad and accepting a four-to-five-month time lapse, but European officials dismissed the offer as a time-wasting gambit aimed at ducking sanctions.

Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad announced that Iran had produced its first batch of uranium enriched to a higher level, telling a crowd at Tehran's Azadi Square that Iran was now a nuclear state while denying that it was manufacturing a bomb.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad warned that Iran will break off all talks over its nuclear programme if new UN sanctions are imposed.

Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad promised that Iran would "respond strongly to any threat" hours before EU foreign ministers were to meet to approve their toughest economic sanctions yet over Iran's nuclear programme.
EU diplomats planned to send low-ranking representatives to Ahmadinejad's first inauguration ceremony without informing Iranian authorities beforehand.
Reformist politician Mehdi Karroubi says international sanctions have strengthened Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's government and assisted its post-election crackdown on the opposition Green movement.
A group of Iranian journalists sympathetic to President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad launched barackobama.ir, a website presenting an Iranian viewpoint on Barack Obama.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad arrived in New York for the UN General Assembly and is conducting interviews with US journalists.

Delegates from the US and European countries walked out of the UN General Assembly during Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's speech after he claimed most nations believed the US government was behind the September 11 attacks.
Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad suggested in his UN General Assembly speech that the 9/11 attacks were an inside job, drawing widespread shock and criticism.
A leaked US embassy cable reports that a source in Ashgabat labeled the announcement of Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's victory in Iran's presidential election a "coup d'etat."
The government of Mahmoud Ahmadinejad introduced a subsidies reform package in Iran, reducing subsidies on major food and energy commodities while providing monthly cash payments.

Iran's opposition green movement leaders call for renewed street protests, referencing the 2009 demonstrations that followed the disputed presidential election giving Mahmoud Ahmadinejad a second term.

Iran's Intelligence Minister Heydar Moslehi was forced to resign after a dispute with President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad and his confidant Esfandiyar Rahim Meshai, but Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei reinstated Moslehi and publicly chastised Ahmadinejad's decision.
A close ally of Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, Esfandiar Rahim Mashaei, is being groomed as a possible successor to the Iranian president when he steps down in two years.

A rift emerges between Mahmoud Ahmadinejad and Supreme Leader Ayatollah Khamenei over the reinstatement of intelligence minister Heydar Moslehi, prompting some Iranian MPs to call for Ahmadinejad's impeachment.

Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad suffers a series of dramatic setbacks in his power struggle with Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei after a failed attempt to challenge the clerical establishment, with his allies arrested and his authority diminished.
Iran's supreme leader Ali Khamenei gave President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad an ultimatum to accept his intervention in a cabinet appointment or resign, amid an unprecedented power struggle.

Mahmoud Ahmadinejad appeared in a cabinet meeting with Intelligence Minister Heydar Moslehi present, under pressure from Ali Khamenei's camp to accept Moslehi's reinstatement, amid an ongoing power struggle.
A top aide in the office of Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad was arrested, amid a power struggle between Ahmadinejad and Supreme Leader Ayatollah Khamenei.

Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad escalated his power struggle with Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei by warning that Khamenei would be powerless without public support, while also clashing with parliament over election oversight and reducing eight ministries to four.

Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's government suffered an unprecedentedly harsh blow to its credibility, with the arrest of officials close to high-ranking cabinet members and an escalating war of words with senior conservatives and Iran's judiciary.

Iranian parliament voted 165-1 to approve a report declaring President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's takeover of the oil ministry an "obvious violation of law" after he sacked the oil minister and declared himself caretaker oil minister.
Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad publicly admitted for the first time a rift between himself and senior figures of the Islamic regime, saying they are "180 degrees away" from him.

Iranian ministers moved closer to impeaching President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad amid clashes with supporters of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, with impeachment proceedings launched against Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Salehi and MPs warning of a motion to impeach Ahmadinejad within 10 days.
Muhammad Sharif Malekzadeh, a close ally of Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, is arrested on financial corruption charges.
Iran's state television censored a video clip of President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad condemning recent arrests of his close allies, prompting his official website to publish the full version.

An Iranian magazine, Shahrvand-e-Emrooz, was closed down, widely believed to be due to a satirical image depicting President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad as an obedient follower of his confidant Esfandiar Rahim Mashaei.
Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad gave a UN speech attacking the US and other major powers as militarist and imperialist, prompting diplomatic walkouts by US, UK, and French delegations.
An Iranian student activist, Peyman Aref, was lashed 74 times for insulting President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, hours before his release from prison.

Iranian judiciary officials attempted to arrest Ali Akbar Javanfekr, a close ally and media adviser to President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, but the arrest was temporarily halted after government intervention.
Iranian censors blocked access to several news websites sympathetic to President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad ahead of parliamentary elections.

The Iranian parliament summons President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad to answer questions over the government's handling of the economy and his personal judgments, an unprecedented move in the history of the Islamic republic.

Early election results indicate conservative rivals of President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad are on course to gain firm control of the Iranian parliament, with his sister Parvin Ahmadinejad defeated in Garmsar.

A video circulated showing a young woman jumping onto Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's car during a provincial visit, drawing international media attention, while his visit to the disputed island of Abu Musa triggered criticism from the UAE and other Persian Gulf states.

Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad suffers a major setback as his supporters fare badly in parliamentary runoff elections, winning only eight of 65 seats while opponents aligned with Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei dominate.
Iranian officials announce that the next presidential election will be held on 14 June 2013, when Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's term will end and he cannot run for a third term.
Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad is due to address the UN General Assembly in what is expected to be his last high-profile international platform before standing down in June 2013.
Ali Akbar Javanfekr, press adviser to President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, was jailed to serve a six-month prison term while Ahmadinejad was addressing the UN general assembly in New York.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad is widely seen as politically finished, as he is banned from standing for a third term and faces mounting criticism over Iran's worsening economic plight.

Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad wrote a letter to judiciary head Sadeq Larijani protesting the judiciary's refusal to allow him to visit Tehran's Evin prison, where his media adviser Ali Akbar Javanfekr is held.

Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, whose contentious presidency will end with a June vote, rejects remarks by a Revolutionary Guards representative about engineering the upcoming elections, saying anyone who wants to direct the Iranian people will be directed by them.
Iranian authorities arrested two journalists and banned three reformist publications, with the arrests linked to an article criticizing President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad repeatedly uses the word "spring" in public remarks, angering conservative rivals who see it as a campaign slogan.

Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, barred from running for a third term, is suspected of campaigning through provincial visits to promote his chief of staff Esfandiar Rahim Mashaei as his favoured successor ahead of the June 14 election.

The editor of an Iranian news website, Ali Ghazali, was arrested after carrying a report claiming that a tape recording existed of President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad discussing vote rigging in the disputed 2009 election, a report Ahmadinejad's office has strongly denied.

Iran began candidate registration for the June presidential election that will mark the end of Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's term, with Ahmadinejad widely suspected to be grooming his chief of staff Esfandiar Rahim Mashaei as a possible successor.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad accompanied his close ally Esfandiar Rahim Mashaei as Mashaei registered as a candidate for Iran's June presidential election, and defended his support for Mashaei amid criticism.
Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, the leading opposition-backed candidate, was disqualified from standing in Iran's presidential election as Mahmoud Ahmadinejad leaves office.

Ahmadinejad expressed dissatisfaction with the Guardian Council's disqualification of his close ally Esfandiar Rahim Mashaei from the presidential election, calling it an act of oppression and promising to raise the issue with Supreme Leader Khamenei.
Iranians vote to elect a successor to Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, with results expected to lead to a runoff.
Hassan Rouhani wins the Iranian presidential election and will succeed Mahmoud Ahmadinejad as president.
Iran's outgoing president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad was summoned to a criminal court in Tehran to answer unspecified charges following Hassan Rouhani's presidential election victory.
The article discusses the 2009 election victory of Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, whose authenticity was cast into doubt, in the context of Hassan Rouhani's 2013 presidential election.
Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei formally endorsed Hassan Rouhani as president, opening the way for Rouhani to take over from Mahmoud Ahmadinejad.
Facebook and Twitter became temporarily accessible in Iran, leading to speculation that the government might lift restrictions imposed during Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's years in office.
Iran's culture minister says books censored or denied publication under former president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's 2006 publishing lockdown will be reviewed again.

Former Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad did not attend the start of his trial in Tehran, where he faces charges including failing to set the structure of the National Iranian Oil Company, delaying the operation of the ministry of youth and sports, and failing to set a budget for the country's metro system.

Mahmoud Ahmadinejad announced he would not run in Iran's 2017 presidential election, submitting to the supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei's indication that his candidacy was not in the country's interests.
Former Iranian president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad registered to run in the upcoming presidential election, defying an edict from Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei not to do so.
Iran’s Guardian Council disqualified former president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad from running in the upcoming presidential election.

facts.text: On 2005-08-23, Iran's conservative-dominated parliament rejected four of President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's proposed cabinet ministers, including oil minister nominee Ali Saeedlou.
On 2005-12-14, Ahmadinejad became the first senior Iranian official to openly deny the Holocaust, calling it a "myth" in a speech in Zahedan.
On 2006-01-11, Ahmadinejad defiantly said Iran would press ahead with its nuclear programme despite international threats and outcry over breaking UN seals at the Natanz enrichment facility.
On 2006-04-10, Mahmoud Ahmadinejad made a triumphal announcement regarding Iran's nuclear program, accompanied by chants of "Death to America" and "Death to Israel."
On 2007-01-17, a majority of Iran's MPs signed an open letter to President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad criticizing his economic policies.
On 2008-03-02, Ahmadinejad arrived in Baghdad on the first state visit of its kind since the 1979 Islamic revolution, pledging a new chapter in relations with Iraq.
On 2009-06-12, official results declared Ahmadinejad winner of Iran's presidential election with 63%, a result disputed by Mir Hossein Mousavi, who alleged the true result showed he won over 60%.
On 2009-11-04, students across Iran planned to lead a huge day of protest against President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's regime, commemorating the 30th anniversary of the US embassy takeover.

event-e310a34200122a1a.summary: Mahmoud Ahmadinejad is widely seen as politically finished, as he is banned from standing for a third term and faces mounting criticism over Iran's worsening economic plight.

event-36538671084a7902.summary: Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad wrote a letter to judiciary head Sadeq Larijani protesting the judiciary's refusal to allow him to visit Tehran's Evin prison, where his media adviser Ali Akbar Javanfekr is held.

event-a65b0f75f4c1ae66.summary: Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, whose contentious presidency will end with a June vote, rejects remarks by a Revolutionary Guards representative about engineering the upcoming elections, saying anyone who wants to direct the Iranian people will be directed by them.

event-efb326a331fd4196.summary: Iranian authorities arrested two journalists and banned three reformist publications, with the arrests linked to an article criticizing President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad.

event-cda5e1670675a256.summary: Mahmoud Ahmadinejad repeatedly uses the word "spring" in public remarks, angering conservative rivals who see it as a campaign slogan.

event-b8a15007d98f001e.summary: Iran began candidate registration for the June presidential election that will mark the end of Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's term, with Ahmadinejad widely suspected to be grooming his chief of staff Esfandiar Rahim Mashaei as a possible successor.

event-41fc536690d076cf.summary: Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, the leading opposition-backed candidate, was disqualified from standing in Iran's presidential election as Mahmoud Ahmadinejad leaves office.

event-febc46ac22f9cc68.summary: Ahmadinejad expressed dissatisfaction with the Guardian Council's disqualification of his close ally Esfandiar Rahim Mashaei from the presidential election, calling it an act of oppression and promising to raise the issue with Supreme Leader Khamenei.

event-cdce0952c1129f7f.summary: Iranians vote to elect a successor to Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, with results expected to lead to a runoff.

event-fb0b1c09a5150076.summary: Hassan Rouhani wins the Iranian presidential election and will succeed Mahmoud Ahmadinejad as president.

event-323fcad7c0c1f20b.summary: Iran's outgoing president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad was summoned to a criminal court in Tehran to answer unspecified charges following Hassan Rouhani's presidential election victory.

event-d03edf76bc59a67c.summary: Facebook and Twitter became temporarily accessible in Iran, leading to speculation that the government might lift restrictions imposed during Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's years in office.

events.summary: Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, as Tehran mayor since 2003, ran for president with an ascetic, man-of-the-people campaign appealing to religious hardliners and working-class conservatives.

Iran's president-elect Mahmoud Ahmadinejad received religious approval from Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, taking his first step toward assuming office ahead of his formal inauguration on Saturday.
Tehran Mayor Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf is re-elected in a vote seen as a sign of waning support for hardline President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad formally began his second term as Iran's president, pledging to serve his people and resist foreign powers questioning the validity of his election.

An article disputes claims that Mahmoud Ahmadinejad has Jewish roots, arguing his family were religious Shia Muslims and that his previous surname Sabourjian derived from carpet-thread painting, not a Jewish prayer shawl.

Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, barred from running for a third term, is suspected of campaigning through provincial visits to promote his chief of staff Esfandiar Rahim Mashaei as his favoured successor ahead of the June 14 election.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad wins Iran's presidential runoff election, defeating Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani.

Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad responded acerbically to Barack Obama's overture to Iran, saying only "fundamental" change from Washington—including a complete withdrawal of US troops worldwide and apologies for past "crimes" against Iran—would be enough to reboot bilateral relations after a 30-year freeze.
Iranian president-elect Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's aides dismiss allegations that he was involved in the 1989 assassination of exiled Kurdish politician Abdul Rahman Ghassemlou in Vienna.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad is described as a presidential candidate and champion of the poor, promising a sharp departure from social freedoms and a crackdown on Western "decadence" if elected.
Iran's new president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad announced the make-up of his cabinet, naming a team of religious conservatives to key ministries.
Iran's outgoing president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad was summoned to a criminal court in Tehran to answer unspecified charges following Hassan Rouhani's presidential election victory.

Iranian politicians discussed abolishing the presidency itself, a move that would affect Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, who would be unable to run for a third term in 2013; Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei hinted he had no problem with plans to scrap the post of president.
Former Iranian president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad registered to run in the upcoming presidential election, defying an edict from Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei not to do so.
Iran’s Guardian Council disqualified former president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad from running in the upcoming presidential election.
Iranian officials announce that the next presidential election will be held on 14 June 2013, when Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's term will end and he cannot run for a third term.

Mahmoud Ahmadinejad announced he would not run in Iran's 2017 presidential election, submitting to the supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei's indication that his candidacy was not in the country's interests.
Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad offers himself as an observer for the 2008 US presidential election, claiming Americans would vote against the current administration in a truly free poll.
An ally of Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad says he has fallen ill due to exhaustion from his heavy workload, amid doubts over whether he will seek re-election in 2009.

Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad suffers a major setback as his supporters fare badly in parliamentary runoff elections, winning only eight of 65 seats while opponents aligned with Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei dominate.
Reformist former Iranian president Mohammed Khatami is close to declaring his candidacy for June's presidential election against incumbent Mahmoud Ahmadinejad.

Mahmoud Ahmadinejad appeared in a cabinet meeting with Intelligence Minister Heydar Moslehi present, under pressure from Ali Khamenei's camp to accept Moslehi's reinstatement, amid an ongoing power struggle.
Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad officially declared that he would run for a second term in the upcoming election.
Ali Akbar Javanfekr, press adviser to President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, was jailed to serve a six-month prison term while Ahmadinejad was addressing the UN general assembly in New York.

Iranian judiciary officials attempted to arrest Ali Akbar Javanfekr, a close ally and media adviser to President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, but the arrest was temporarily halted after government intervention.
A top aide in the office of Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad was arrested, amid a power struggle between Ahmadinejad and Supreme Leader Ayatollah Khamenei.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad denied the existence of homosexuals in Iran at Columbia University, prompting journalist Siamak Ghaderi to conduct interviews with Iranian homosexuals.

Mahmoud Ahmadinejad traveled to Yekaterinburg, Russia for a Shanghai Co-operation Organisation summit amid anti-government protests over Iran's disputed presidential election, where the SCO formally congratulated him on his landslide win.

Iran's Intelligence Minister Heydar Moslehi was forced to resign after a dispute with President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad and his confidant Esfandiyar Rahim Meshai, but Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei reinstated Moslehi and publicly chastised Ahmadinejad's decision.
Iranian censors blocked access to several news websites sympathetic to President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad ahead of parliamentary elections.

Ahmadinejad's supporters apparently failed to win control of key councils in elections, with his Sweet Scent of Service coalition winning only three of 15 Tehran city council seats, while critic Hashemi Rafsanjani received the most votes in elections to the experts' assembly.

events.summary: Iranian officials announce that the next presidential election will be held on 14 June 2013, when Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's term will end and he cannot run for a third term.

Iran began candidate registration for the June presidential election that will mark the end of Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's term, with Ahmadinejad widely suspected to be grooming his chief of staff Esfandiar Rahim Mashaei as a possible successor.

Iranian politicians discussed abolishing the presidency itself, a move that would affect Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, who would be unable to run for a third term in 2013; Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei hinted he had no problem with plans to scrap the post of president.
Iran’s Guardian Council disqualified former president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad from running in the upcoming presidential election.
Former Iranian president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad registered to run in the upcoming presidential election, defying an edict from Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei not to do so.
Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad officially declared that he would run for a second term in the upcoming election.
Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei told a cabinet meeting that President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad should prepare for a second term in office ahead of June's presidential election.

Mahmoud Ahmadinejad hails his contested re-election as a victory for the Iranian people and a defeat for the enemies of the Islamic Republic, after the Guardian Council confirmed his defeat of challenger Mir Hossein Mousavi.

Mahmoud Ahmadinejad announced he would not run in Iran's 2017 presidential election, submitting to the supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei's indication that his candidacy was not in the country's interests.

Iranian media report that Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, winner of the disputed presidential election, is to be sworn in before parliament between 26 July and 19 August, after Iran's top electoral authority rules out annulling the result.
Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei formally endorsed Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's second term as president, seven weeks after disputed elections prompted mass protests.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad is sworn in for a second term as Iranian president amid opposition walkouts, demonstrations, and protests.
Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, the leading opposition-backed candidate, was disqualified from standing in Iran's presidential election as Mahmoud Ahmadinejad leaves office.
Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad offers himself as an observer for the 2008 US presidential election, claiming Americans would vote against the current administration in a truly free poll.
Iranian voters went to the polls to elect local councils and the Assembly of Experts in the first test of President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's popularity since he took office.

Mahmoud Ahmadinejad appeared in a cabinet meeting with Intelligence Minister Heydar Moslehi present, under pressure from Ali Khamenei's camp to accept Moslehi's reinstatement, amid an ongoing power struggle.
Reformist former Iranian president Mohammed Khatami is close to declaring his candidacy for June's presidential election against incumbent Mahmoud Ahmadinejad.

Iran's fundamentalist-dominated parliament passes a law severely restricting political advertising for the March 2008 parliamentary elections, which are expected to test Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's popularity.

Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, barred from running for a third term, is suspected of campaigning through provincial visits to promote his chief of staff Esfandiar Rahim Mashaei as his favoured successor ahead of the June 14 election.
President George W. Bush appoints former Presidents George H.W. Bush and Bill Clinton to lead a joint appeal for emergency donations to victims of the Indian Ocean tsunami.
A close ally of Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, Esfandiar Rahim Mashaei, is being groomed as a possible successor to the Iranian president when he steps down in two years.
Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei publicly endorses Mahmoud Ahmadinejad for a new four-year presidential term, ahead of his formal swearing-in on Wednesday.
Ali Akbar Javanfekr, press adviser to President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, was jailed to serve a six-month prison term while Ahmadinejad was addressing the UN general assembly in New York.
A top aide in the office of Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad was arrested, amid a power struggle between Ahmadinejad and Supreme Leader Ayatollah Khamenei.
Reformist politician Mehdi Karroubi says international sanctions have strengthened Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's government and assisted its post-election crackdown on the opposition Green movement.

Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad warned his opponents against detaining any members of his cabinet, calling recent arrests of his close allies politically motivated and vowing to defend his government.
Iranian censors blocked access to several news websites sympathetic to President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad ahead of parliamentary elections.

Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's government suffered an unprecedentedly harsh blow to its credibility, with the arrest of officials close to high-ranking cabinet members and an escalating war of words with senior conservatives and Iran's judiciary.
Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei overruled President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad by ordering him to supply cheap gas to villages amid power cuts during an unusually harsh winter.
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad repeatedly uses the word "spring" in public remarks, angering conservative rivals who see it as a campaign slogan.

Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad is expected to use his speech to the UN General Assembly to appeal to a domestic audience and bolster his leadership amid isolation and disputes with Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

existing_events.summary: Iran's state television censored a video clip of President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad condemning recent arrests of his close allies, prompting his official website to publish the full version.

An Iranian court acquits former nuclear negotiator Hossein Mousavian of spying for the British government but convicts him of acting against the Islamic authorities, after President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad had called him a "spy" and "traitor."

Early election results indicate conservative rivals of President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad are on course to gain firm control of the Iranian parliament, with his sister Parvin Ahmadinejad defeated in Garmsar.
A censorship crackdown instigated by President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad led to the banning of dozens of literary masterpieces and international bestsellers in Iran.

150 Iranian parliamentarians signed a letter blaming President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad for raging inflation and high unemployment and criticizing his government's failure to deliver the budget on time.

Iranian students protested against President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad at Tehran's Amir Kabir university, burning his picture and chanting "Death to the dictator," in the first sign of open dissent since he took office.

Iranian students who protested against President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad in December have been expelled from Tehran's Amir Kabir University and earmarked for compulsory military service in an apparent act of official retribution.

European Union ambassadors in Tehran jointly agreed to boycott Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's inauguration as president after the disputed 2009 election, though only Sweden's ambassador ultimately attended.

Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad officially declared that he would run for a second term in the upcoming election.

Iran announces it has successfully enriched uranium to a new level of 4.8%, a month after President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad revealed enrichment to 3.6%.
